clue.text: The wearing of the green should be prevented by this notice

definitions.text: The wearing of the green should be prevented by this notice

parts.words: The wearing of the green should be prevented by this notice
parts.note: the wearing of the green sounds like Irish patriotism, but here it means feet wearing down a lawn, which a park sign forbids

explanation.surface: A notice banning a display of Irish green, as if patriotism were outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Wearing of the Green' is an Irish ballad; the clue reads the phrase literally, as turf being worn away by walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A park sign telling people not to walk on the lawn stops the turf being trodden bare.

clue.text: When robbers start or finish work?

definitions.text: When robbers start or finish work?

parts.words: When robbers start or finish work
parts.note: to knock off is slang both for stealing and for stopping work, so a thief's start of work is everyone else's end of it

explanation.surface: Asking at what hour criminals clock on and clock off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock off' means both 'rob' (British slang) and 'stop work for the day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of the working day is when employees down tools, which in slang also describes thieves setting about stealing.

clue.text: Insist upon new corn fee

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the two following words are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A farmer demanding a fresh charge on grain.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel observance of a rule is to insist on it being followed.

clue.text: A never-to be-repeated occasion

parts.note: an event that happens a single time and no more is described here as a one-off

explanation.definitionFit: Something done on just one occasion happens a single time, and the adverb names that one time.

clue.text: Presumptuous footballer?

definitions.meaning: bold or overfamiliar, too pushy in manner
an attacking player in football, a striker; the question mark flags the example

explanation.definitionFit: Both an overbold manner and an attacking position in the football team share the word.

clue.text: Last offer

definitions.meaning: to last is to endure or keep going
to offer something is to extend it towards someone

explanation.definitionFit: Supplies holding up mean they endure, and extending a hand with something in it is presenting it.

clue.text: Gravity-free network

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity or gravitational acceleration
to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A web of connections in which nothing is weighed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a lattice of crossing lines, such as the electricity distribution system.

clue.text: Notice a wild plant

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the two preceding words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spotting an untamed plant growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a poisonous flowering herb.

clue.text: Steps taken quietly

parts.note: steps sounds like footfalls of someone creeping, but means dance steps done in soft-soled footwear

explanation.definitionFit: It is a tap-style dance performed in soft-soled shoes, sliding the feet with little noise.

clue.text: Member of the police force, if trained

indicators.note: trained means the letters of the words force and if are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A police constable is someone who joined the force and was properly trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' sits naturally beside 'police', but it is fodder: 'trained' rearranges FORCEIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable or inspector is a rank-holding member of the constabulary.

clue.text: Stopped and fired

definitions.meaning: ceased or let up, as rain or an attack might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both easing up on something and making workers redundant.

clue.text: Church of Scotland

parts.note: the Scottish word for a church building, and also the name for the national Presbyterian church

explanation.definitionFit: In Scots the word for a church building is also used for the national Presbyterian church itself.

clue.text: Travel in colourless form of transport

indicators.note: in places the word for travel inside the word for colourless

parts.note: wan means pale or colourless
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Getting about in a drab, grey vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a horse-drawn cart or a railway goods vehicle.

clue.text: Bringer of love and life?

parts.note: an act of affection and also the mouth-to-mouth resuscitation called by the same name 'of life'

explanation.definitionFit: Lips meeting express affection, and the resuscitation technique is called the 'of life' version of it.

clue.text: A classical type

parts.note: the classical Greek equivalent of the letter A, a character or piece of type

explanation.definitionFit: It is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of the Roman A.

clue.text: It's possibly rated as skilled employment

indicators.note: possibly hints the word rated may be a jumble of something else

explanation.surface: A craft job that may be graded as skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual occupation such as plumbing or carpentry is called a craft or a line of work.

clue.text: Outside left required to be prodded into action

indicators.note: outside says the word for required wraps round the letter for left

parts.note: needed means required

explanation.surface: A footballer playing outside left needed a push to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' looks like a football wing position, but 'Outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be goaded or provoked is to be pricked as if with a sharp point.

clue.text: Wild toper at a party could be lethal

definitions.note: the definition describes the weapon by what it can do, rather than naming a noun

indicators.note: wild means the letters of toper are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A drunk running amok at a party might be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges TOPER to TORPE. A toper is a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is a weapon designed to sink ships, so it can kill.

clue.text: Friendly approach to make up for a former roughness

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
a chap is a crack or roughness of the skin, as in chapped hands

explanation.surface: Making amends for past coarse behaviour with a warm greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make up for a' is link wording: the answer is made up from the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an affectionate form of address, the way one might hail a friend.

clue.text: See the bishop's concern

definitions.meaning: a see is a bishop's seat or jurisdiction
the area a bishop is responsible for

explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the noun for a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's district of churches is both the see and what he oversees.

clue.text: Queue of ill-mannered person and dog

parts.note: a pig is a rude or greedy person
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A line of people containing a boor and his hound.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue (cue) is an old word for a braid of hair hanging at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is a plait of hair worn hanging behind the head.

clue.text: Fair play for car-drivers

parts.note: fair is a funfair, not justice, and the play is a ride where people steer little cars and bump

explanation.surface: A call for road users to treat each other justly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at a funfair are an amusement ride where riders steer small electric vehicles.

clue.text: She puts on other people's clothes

definitions.text: She puts on other people's clothes

parts.words: She puts on other people's clothes
parts.note: sounds like someone wearing borrowed garments, but means a theatre assistant who helps actors into costume

explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre an assistant helps performers into their costumes.

clue.text: Time of day for ironing things out

explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day before night, and also the act of levelling or smoothing.

clue.text: Run loud and deep

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction for loud
low means deep, as of a voice

explanation.surface: A river runs noisy and deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Water moving steadily along streams onward.

clue.text: Looked, started to go back, then went ahead

indicators.note: back says the short word go is turned round

parts.note: led means went ahead or in front

explanation.surface: Someone who started to retreat and then pressed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG. 'started to' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at with desire, a particular way of looking.

clue.text: It's neckwear, say, for the dandy

indicators.note: say signals that the word for neckwear is spoken aloud

parts.note: a bow is a bow tie, worn at the neck

explanation.surface: A foppish man wearing a cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a fashionable man, a fop or ladies' man.

clue.text: School is to go in two directions

indicators.note: go in says the word to is placed inside the letters for the two compass points

parts.note: E and N are east and north

explanation.surface: A school that cannot decide which way to head.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English fee-paying boarding establishment.

clue.text: Offbeat classical character following

indicators.note: off attached to beat says the rhythm word is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: An unconventional Greek figure coming next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' within 'Offbeat' rearranges BEAT. 'following' is link wording, apt as it is the second Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Sluggish movement of a train that's vanished

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective while the answer is the noun for that state

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of a train and the abbreviation for 'that is' are shifted around
vanished says one letter A of the shuffled pool disappears, leaving the rest to form the answer

parts.note: taken as written
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A train crawling along after the one in front has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement of' rearranges A TRAIN plus IE; 'vanished' removes one A from that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is lethargy or reluctance to move, the state of being torpid.

clue.text: She's got a phrase of music officer

parts.note: taken as written; the 's stands for has, joining the next piece
a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A woman has a tune for a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHERIFF is a law officer: in the US a county's chief of police.
explanation.definitionFit: A county law enforcement official in America, or a ceremonial post in England.

clue.text: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups?

definitions.text: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups?

parts.words: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups
parts.note: figure suggests 'feature', but also means a geometric shape, and always means everlasting

explanation.surface: Asking whether a third party is always behind a divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a love affair involving three people, a common cause of divorce.
